'''Jacques Distler''' (born January 1, 1961) is a Canadian-born American [[physicist]] working in [[string theory]]. He has been a professor of [[physics]] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] since 1994.

==Early life and education==
Distler was born to a Jewish family in [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]], Canada, where he attended [[Herzliah High School]] ([[Snowdon, Montreal|Snowdon]]). He earned his bachelor's and doctoral degrees at [[Harvard University]]. His 1987 thesis ''Compactified String Theories'' was supervised by [[Sidney Coleman]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=93820|title=Jacques Joseph Distler}}</ref>

==Physics career==
Before going to Texas, he was assistant professor at [[Princeton University]].

According to citation counts, his most influential publication is his 1989 paper on [[conformal field theory]] in two dimensions.  His earliest paper is ''Gauge Invariant Superstring Field Theory,'' co-authored with André LeClair and published in 1986 in Nuclear Physics B.

He has studied the "[[string theory landscape|landscape]]" of [[Metastability|metastable]] [[False vacuum|vacua]] in string theory. In July 2005, he released a paper on this topic.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0507090 Random polynomials and the friendly landscape] July 2005, arXiv.org</ref>  Professor Distler was a member of arXiv's physics advisory board.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/help/physics/#AdvisoryCommittee arXiv advisory board]</ref>{{failed verification|date=April 2018}}

He maintains a [[blog]] titled ''Musings: Thoughts on Science, Computing, and Life on Earth''.<ref>{{cite web |title= Musings: Thoughts on Science, Computing, and Life on Earth|url=https://golem.ph.utexas.edu/~distler/blog/}}</ref>

In 2026, Distler was named a [[Lists of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]], "for seminal contributions to string theory and quantum field theory, including the Distler-Kawai formulation of two-dimensional quantum gravity and Liouville theory, foundational work on heterotic string compactifications, and advances in the structure of superconformal field theories".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=distler&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=November 2, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Distler maintains a [http://golem.ph.utexas.edu/~distler/shoah/ webpage] dedicated to his father, who was born in [[Poland]] and escaped the German slave camps of [[World War II]].
